name: Haworth
notes: One of nine refined crewed south-pole landing candidate regions NASA announced on Oct 28, 2024 (originally for Artemis III; the first landing is now planned for Artemis IV). Named for nearby Haworth crater, but NASA did not publish a region-center coordinate.

name: Peak near Cabeus B
notes: One of nine refined crewed south-pole landing candidate regions NASA announced on Oct 28, 2024 (originally for Artemis III; the first landing is now planned for Artemis IV), in no priority order. Each region contains multiple potential landing sites. NASA published names and a map, not a single center coordinate. No later official replacement list was found as of Nov 11, 2026. In 2026 NASA redesignated Artemis III as a low-Earth-orbit test; this remains the last official public candidate set for the first south-pole crewed landing.

name: Apollo 16
notes: Lunar Module at Descartes. Planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421. Coordinates from LRO images; Wagner et al., Icarus 283, 92–103 (2017), as compiled by NASA NSSDC.

name: Connecting Ridge
notes: Informal name (Shackleton–de Gerlache Connecting Ridge); not in the IAU gazetteer. Coordinates are the published center of LROC NAC DTM product NAC\_DTM\_SHACKRDGE02, not a surveyed peak. Product coverage is about 89.37°S–89.63°S, 209.81°E–239.10°E.

name: Apollo 15
notes: Lunar Module at Hadley Rille. Planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421. Coordinates from LRO images; Wagner et al., Icarus 283, 92–103 (2017), as compiled by NASA NSSDC.

name: Apollo 17

name: Malapert massif
notes: IAU name Mons Malapert (Feature 16338), approved Aug 26, 2024; LOLA 2011 control network; diameter 67 km. This is the named mountain, not a published center of the Artemis “Malapert Massif” region polygon.

name: Apollo 14
notes: Lunar Module at Fra Mauro. Planetocentric Mean Earth/Polar Axis, DE421. Coordinates from LRO images; Wagner et al., Icarus 283, 92–103 (2017), as compiled by NASA NSSDC.

name: Malapert Massif
notes: One of nine refined crewed south-pole landing candidate regions NASA announced on Oct 28, 2024 (originally for Artemis III; the first landing is now planned for Artemis IV). Distinct from the IAU-named mountain Mons Malapert, whose gazetteer center is listed in the notable-features section. NASA did not publish a region-center coordinate.

name: de Gerlache rim
notes: IAU crater-center coordinates from the USGS Gazetteer (Feature 1439, de Gerlache; planetographic, +East; diameter 32.71 km). No single official rim-point coordinate is published. Distinct from the Artemis region “de Gerlache Rim 2,” which has no published center.

name: Mons Mouton Plateau
notes: One of nine refined crewed south-pole landing candidate regions NASA announced on Oct 28, 2024 (originally for Artemis III; the first landing is now planned for Artemis IV). Distinct from the Mons Mouton region and from the IAU-named Mons Mouton (gazetteer center 84.60°S, 31.00°E). NASA did not publish a region-center coordinate.

name: Nobile Rim 2
notes: One of nine refined crewed south-pole landing candidate regions NASA announced on Oct 28, 2024 (originally for Artemis III; the first landing is now planned for Artemis IV). Named for the rim of Nobile crater. NASA did not publish a region-center coordinate.

name: Mons Mouton
notes: One of nine refined crewed south-pole landing candidate regions NASA announced on Oct 28, 2024 (originally for Artemis III; the first landing is now planned for Artemis IV). The IAU feature Mons Mouton (Feature 16070) has a gazetteer center of 84.60°S, 31.00°E, but that is the named mountain, not a published center of this landing region.

name: de Gerlache Rim 2
notes: One of nine refined crewed south-pole landing candidate regions NASA announced on Oct 28, 2024 (originally for Artemis III; the first landing is now planned for Artemis IV). Kept from the original 2022 set of 13. Distinct from the IAU crater de Gerlache, whose center is listed in the notable-features section. NASA did not publish a region-center coordinate.

name: Shackleton rim
notes: IAU crater-center coordinates from the USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature (Feature 5450, Shackleton; planetographic, +East; diameter 20.92 km). No single official coordinate is published for a specific point on the rim; the rim lies roughly one radius (\~10 km) from this center.
